model: Gas monitors 22G (CO, NO2, CO2, refrigerant and others)
applies_to: Belimo 22G..-5A and 22G..-5B wall gas monitors (CO, NO2, CO2, NH3, refrigerant and other gases) with CAN bus and BACnet MS/TP.
summary: Belimo 22G gas monitors measure one or two gases and drive local relays and alarms. The -A and -B models have a BACnet MS/TP port that serves the local gas readings, ambient temperature, an auxiliary input and the alarm/relay states. With menu setting 46 = 2 one monitor also acts as a gateway and publishes the gas readings of every monitor on its CAN bus.
notes: Only the fixed objects are listed. With menu setting 46 = 2, each CAN bus monitor adds 'AV XYY - Gas reading XYY', where X = 1 for sensor A (top) or 2 for sensor B (bottom) and YY = the CAN bus address.
AV 0 and AV 1 are for setting 46 = 1; AV 1 needs a second sensor.
Each gas reading object carries the gas type and scale in its description.
BACnet MS/TP is only on -A and -B models; -C models are CAN bus only.

integration.summary: Turn on BACnet with menu setting 46, set the MS/TP address, baud and device instance at the keypad, then read the gas readings and the three alarm objects. Use setting 46 = 2 on one -A or -B monitor to bring a whole CAN bus network into the BMS.
integration.enable: Menu setting 46: 0 = BACnet off, 1 = BACnet on, 2 = BACnet on plus all CAN bus gas readings.
setup: MS/TP address 0-127, set at the keypad.
Baud 9600, 19200, 38400 or 76800; power cycle after a change.
Device instance is entered in two parts at the keypad (1000-4,194,303, then 0-999).
Set the maximum MAC address no lower than the highest address on the network, or devices are hidden.
EOL jumpers go ON only on the first and last devices.
gotchas: Gas reading objects appear only when menu setting 46 is 1 or 2.
A menu setting can make CAN bus alarms and relays follow BACnet alarms on the gateway monitor.

source.title: Belimo Gas Monitors Operating Manual, 6.2 PICS: BACnet MS/TP
